thesis: This is an update to the TLT long opened 2026-11-04 at 80.30, now 82.24 (+2.4%), and the decision is hold with levels unchanged. The original thesis was duration into a slowing economy; what has actually happened is better than that. With a December hike ~92% priced, the long end is trading as a bull flattener rather than a bear steepener: 10y-2y compressed from +0.28 to +0.24 in a single session while TLT made a higher high, which is the tape saying a credible inflation-fighting Fed caps the long end rather than lifting it. From 82.24 the target is +2.1% away and the stop -4.2%, so the remaining distribution is better than it was at entry.
key_risk: The 10-year real yield near 2.88% is at cycle highs and a hawkish dot plot or a 50bp surprise on Dec 9 re-steepens the curve and takes TLT through 79 in days. A secondary risk is that the stop at 78.80 sits 1.88 ATR from entry against an 1.8 ATR ETF floor — it clears, but barely, so a modest rise in realised vol would make this a stop too tight to publish fresh.
counter_argument: If inflation is genuinely re-accelerating — core PCE +3.8% y/y in October, and the Fed minutes record participants open to more than 25bp — then the long end should demand more term premium, not less, and every duration long in 2026 has been wrong. The answer is that this is why the position is held rather than added to, and why it has a time stop: the bull-flattener claim is falsifiable by Dec 19.

thesis: Update to the HUN long opened 2026-11-10 at 9.00, now 9.29 (+3.2%); decision is hold with levels unchanged, and two things have changed since publication. First, on 2026-11-25 USTR proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies over structural excess capacity in manufacturing, with chemicals among the sectors named — overcapacity out of Asia is the single line item that de-rated HUN 42% from its 120-day high, so an action aimed at it is a change in the thing that broke the stock, not a new story. HUN closed +6.2% at 9.29 on the heaviest volume in a month on a day the Nasdaq was down 4% intraday. Second, the all-stock merger of equals with Olin has cleared both shareholder votes and the HSR waiting period and is expected to close Q1 2027. Market cap $1.63B with $27.1M average daily dollar volume, so exit is not the constraint at a 2% position.
key_risk: The merger is the dominant fact and it cuts both ways: HUN holders inherit Olin's balance sheet, which carried $2,798.3M of net debt at 5.2x adjusted EBITDA on 2026-09-30 (up from 3.7x a year earlier), and Olin guided Q4 2026 adjusted EBITDA to $80-100M against Q3's $191.4M — a ~50% sequential fall that annualises leverage toward 7x, into a Fed the market says hikes on Dec 9. Second risk: the tariffs are proposals with no stated effective date, so this is a policy re-rating that can simply not happen. Third: the 8.09 stop sits below the 2026-11-23 pivot of 8.32 but ABOVE the 120-day low of 7.995, so a full retest of that low stops the position out.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that US commodity chemical producers are large net exporters and Section 301 invites retaliation, so the tariff is not unambiguously good for them; and in epoxy specifically the US already terminated its China and India antidumping cases on a USITC negligible-imports finding, so the China read-through is thinner than the headline. Answered partly: HUN's own CEO put $981,000 of his own money into the open market at 9.81 on 2026-08-03, after the merger was announced — he is the person who knows both the retaliation exposure and the combined balance sheet, and he bought above today's price.

thesis: Update to the HII long opened 2026-10-12 at 262.00, now 299.34 (+14.3%), and the decision is hold with a trailing plan added rather than a level moved. The reason to publish it rather than leave it alone is that the position had no risk management in place: 48% of the distance from entry to target has been covered while the hard stop sat 20.3% below the market, so a full round trip was costless to the tracker and expensive to the holder. HII is also doing the one thing that justifies holding it — outperforming both the market and its own sector on every window measured (1m +13.3 vs SPY and +6.4 vs ITA, 3m +7.7 and +12.6, 6m -1.7 and +5.7), which is leadership inside a lagging group rather than a rising tide.
key_risk: The 339.76 target is above the 120-day high of 334.53, so the last leg needs a new high rather than a retrace, and at a 3.53% daily ATR the 288-302 chop of the last two weeks can take out a trailing exit without the thesis changing. The published 0.45 win probability sits 21.8 points above the 0.232 that 3.31:1 implies, which is a large claimed edge and should be read carefully — see the counter-argument for why the entry-based baseline understates a position already half-way to its target.
counter_argument: Three officers sold $5.61M in the last six months with no open-market purchases, which is weak evidence alone but is not nothing when the stock is up 14% — the people closest to the backlog are taking money off the table, and that is the main argument for trimming half at 325 rather than waiting for 339.76. On the win probability: a driftless walk from the *current* 299.34 touches 339.76 before 238.50 with probability 60.84/(40.42+60.84) = 60%, so 0.45 is conservative against where the position actually stands; it is only a large claim against a baseline computed from an entry taken six weeks ago.

evidence.detail: Relative strength measured against both SPY and ITA, its own sector ETF: HII +6.41% absolute over 1m while SPY fell 6.88% and ITA was flat at +0.04% — outperforming its sector by 6.37 points on 1m, 12.62 on 3m and 5.70 on 6m. Leadership inside a group that is itself lagging.

The trail level is the 2026-11-20 swing low of 279.80, with the 50-day at 282.11 sitting just above it; the trim level 325.00 is set below the 120-day high of 334.53. ATR14 is 10.58 (3.53%), so 279.80 is 1.85 ATR below the 299.34 close — outside ordinary noise rather than inside it.
